judgements.justification: Both committees brought literature: A named 2020 lightweight SR baselines, B's DsQ3 named prior SR pruning work and HRank; the gap is different literature (R07), not one committee lacking it.
A's meta-review said 'the authors seem to agree' that improvements are fairly small, which the forum record does not show, pushing toward the reject.
No reviewer or AC in either committee raised breadth of audience or venue fit.
A rejected and B followed unanimous 8s; no misreading detractor kept a chair arguing only acceptance.
Only B's chSU asked about weight normalization and sensitivity; the new ablation and sensitivity tables (and HRank for DsQ3) satisfied it and B's scores rose, while A never saw them.
A's only confidence-5 reviewer, k8sL, spent 1 hour on a three-sentence review and fell to 5; no expert review was outweighed.
k8sL's 2021-08-27 cut rested on novelty and LatticeNet points already raised and answered in the rebuttal, not a new unanswerable objection.
A's 4s carried critical texts and B's 8s carried strong praise; the rating gap matches different verbal assessments, not leniency.
A faulted novelty communication and small gains, not an overstated headline claim; neither committee narrowed the 'first attempt' claim.
No committee converged on marginal-accept scores: A rated 5, 4, 4 and B 8, 8, 8 at confidence 5.
